items.title: Cross-User OAuth 2.0 Account Linking & Jira Cloud Token/Notification Hijacking in httpOAuth2Complete
items.confidence: 100% (Verified in Source + Contradicts Sibling OAuth1a & GitHub Plugin Guards)
items.summary: In mattermost/mattermost-plugin-jira, the Jira Cloud OAuth 2.0 callback endpoint (GET /instance/{id}/oauth2/complete.html, handled by httpOAuth2Complete in server/user_cloud_oauth.go:22-91) is registered without the p.checkAuth middleware (server/http.go:126) and never checks r.Header.Get("Mattermost-User-Id"). Instead, it extracts mattermostUserID := stateArray[1] directly from the state query parameter (<random15>_<mattermostUserID>) and binds the victim's Jira Cloud OAuth 2.0 access_token and refresh_token (offline_access) to stateArray[1]. Furthermore, CodeVerifier and CodeChallenge in server/instance_cloud_oauth.go:74-86 are generated once at instance installation time and shared across all users.
items.whySolid: In the exact same file (server/http.go:122) and sibling handler (httpOAuth1aComplete in server/user_server.go:61), OAuth 1.0a enforces p.checkAuth and reads mattermostUserID := r.Header.Get("Mattermost-User-Id"). Similarly, mattermost-plugin-github (server/plugin/api.go:164, 408) enforces p.checkAuth and verifies state.UserID == c.UserID. Omitting both checks in httpOAuth2Complete allows an attacker who generates a valid state token for their own Mattermost account to trick a victim into authorizing the Mattermost Jira app, linking the victim's Jira Cloud tokens and Jira DM notifications directly to the attacker's Mattermost account.
items.remediation: Wrap routeOAuth2Complete in p.checkAuth(...) in server/http.go:126, verify r.Header.Get("Mattermost-User-Id") == mattermostUserID in httpOAuth2Complete before loading the one-time secret or exchanging the code, and generate per-flow PKCE CodeVerifier values stored in otsStore.
items.disclosedVia: Disclosed to responsibledisclosure@mattermost.com (Resend ID: 01a15d35-c4b8-7e2c-bf83-dce79c6f7d34, CC: business@nullai.tech)

items.title: Arbitrary Host File Disclosure via dereference: true Symlink Following in copyDir & npx skills use
items.confidence: 100% (Verified in Source + Contradicts Sibling Module Guards)
items.summary: In src/installer.ts:542-563 (copyDir) and src/use.ts:577-610 (copySkillFiles), skills cloned via Git are copied into the project workspace using cp(srcPath, destPath, { dereference: true, recursive: true }). A developer comment on line 553 explicitly notes '// Skip broken symlinks (e.g., pointing to absolute paths on another machine) instead of aborting the entire install', catching ENOENT when a symlink target is missing. However, when the target path DOES exist on the user's or CI runner's machine (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, /etc/passwd, or ../../../../.env), dereference: true follows the symlink and copies the victim's host file into .agents/skills/<skill>/ or prints it to stdout during npx skills use.
items.whySolid: Sibling modules in the exact same repo (src/download-source.ts:106 and src/providers/wellknown.ts:291) explicitly block symlinks ('Archive links are not supported') and enforce path containment. The developer comment on line 553 proves symlinks in remote Git repos were considered for availability (ENOENT) but missed for confidentiality.
items.remediation: Resolve realpath(srcPath) before copying and verify it remains strictly inside realpath(skillRootDir) using isSubpathSafe(), or reject symbolic links (entry.isSymbolicLink()) in copyDir and copySkillFiles.
items.disclosedVia: Disclosed to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com (Resend ID: 01a15cf8-cda2-7cea-b848-28ed0435e44d, CC: business@nullai.tech)

items.title: Git Option Injection (--upload-pack / -c) via Disabled simple-git Guards & Missing '--' in cloneRepo
items.confidence: 100% (Verified in Source + Explicit Developer Comment Mismatch)
items.summary: createGitClient() in src/git.ts:194-216 disables all 19 simple-git safety guards (including allowUnsafePack: true, allowUnsafeProtocolOverride: true, allowUnsafeHooksPath: true) based on the comment on lines 190-192 claiming 'the clone URL and ref cannot configure them'. However, cloneRepo(url, ref) on line 295 only checks if (/^ext::/i.test(url)), never rejects url or ref values starting with '-', and omits '--' (end-of-options) when calling git.clone(url, tempDir, cloneOptions). Meanwhile, src/update.ts:729-733 explicitly documents that skills-lock.json is an untrusted attack surface ('influenceable by whoever publishes a skill'), yet line 881 passes entry.sourceUrl and entry.ref from skills-lock.json directly into cloneRepo.
items.whySolid: Sibling functions in the same file (tryGhClone on line 255 and getGitTreeHash on line 401) explicitly pass '--' to prevent option injection, proving its omission in cloneRepo alongside allowUnsafePack: true is a concrete security oversight.
items.remediation: Reject any url or ref starting with '-' in cloneRepo() and append '--' to cloneOptions before the positional url and tempDir arguments.
items.disclosedVia: Disclosed to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com (Resend ID: 01a15cf8-cda2-7cea-b848-28ed0435e44d, CC: business@nullai.tech)

items.title: SAML Validation Contract Bypass: NaN Timestamp Expiration Bypass, CDATA Differential & Missing Multi-Element Checks
items.summary: Consolidated 3 concrete validation bypasses in stytchauth/samlshield: (1) In src/validate.ts:994-1021, Date.parse(notOnOrAfter) and Date.parse(notBefore) are never checked for Number.isNaN(); in JavaScript, NaN <= now and NaN > nbTime both evaluate to false, silently passing expired or malformed timestamps. (2) In src/validate.ts:140-152, strictTextContent() only collects NodeType.TEXT_NODE (3) and ignores NodeType.CDATA_SECTION_NODE (4), whereas @node-saml/node-saml concatenates both—creating a parser differential on <NameID>, <Issuer>, and <Audience> elements containing CDATA sections. (3) Subject (line 953), Conditions (line 977), and SignatureValue (line 868) check strict.length > 1 but omit liberal.length > 1.
items.whySolid: Directly violates the contract testing invariants documented in CONTRACT_TESTING.md and README.md.
items.remediation: Check Number.isNaN(noaTime) / Number.isNaN(nbTime), include NodeType.CDATA_SECTION_NODE in strictTextContent(), and enforce liberal.length === 1 on Subject, Conditions, and SignatureValue.
items.disclosedVia: GitHub Advisory GHSA-h4pw-wj8w-qh2h + Email to security@stytch.com (Resend ID: 01a15cf8-cdfa-769f-9a2b-93edf7265034)

items.title: Doppler CLI Windows updateViaWinget Version Argument & Local Fallback PBKDF2 Iteration Count
items.severity: Low / Informational (Held Back — Do Not Submit)
items.summary: In pkg/controllers/upgrade.go, updateViaWinget passes version.ProgramVersion to exec.Command('cmd.exe', '/C', 'winget upgrade --id Doppler.doppler --version '+version). However, this version string is fetched over HTTPS from Doppler's own cli.doppler.com server and parsed through version.Normalize(). Similarly, the 5,000-round PBKDF2 fallback in pkg/crypto/aes.go is only triggered if passphrase.DeriveKey returns an error.
items.whySolid: HELD BACK IN 'POSSIBLE / NOT SURE': Submitting this would look weak because exploiting updateViaWinget requires already compromising Doppler's official release server. Kept strictly as internal documentation.
items.remediation: Pass arguments directly to exec.Command('winget', 'upgrade', '--id', 'Doppler.doppler', '--version', version) without cmd.exe /C, and fail closed if passphrase.DeriveKey errors.
